 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 09-07-2021 at about 09.25 a.m, the rider of the Honda Dio Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-01-HX-8284 was proceeding in front of Police vehicle No.112 and the rider of the Motor Cycle without given any signal, suddenly came to the right side and has stopped the vehicle near Maruthi Showroom, Attibele - Sarjapura Road, Sarjapura,
Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of Police (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 vehicle No.112

in order to avoid the accident to the Motor Cycle, lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the divider and in turn to the electrical pole which was in the middle of the divider and to the Maruthi Swift Car No.KA-03-MF-2099 which was coming from the right side and the said car turtled.

Due to the negligent driving of Devendra vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166858572/
2 the 112 Police vehicle driver, the electrical pole broken and fallen on the Tata Ace vehicle which was coming from the opposite direction and the Tata Ace also severely damaged and the occupants are also sustained grievous severe injuries, in which petitioner Devendra was an occupant and petitioner sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was taken to Town hospital, Sarjapura, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 09.07.2021 to 14.07.2021 for about 6 days and has undergone operation and taken treatment, as the injuries were severe the operation done was complicated, the petitioner was kept under treatment in the hospital and presently the petitioner under treatment.

Due to the grievous injuries and hospitalization the petitioner has undergone enormous pain, suffering and mental agony and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, treatment and Rs.50,000/-
towards incidental expenses and at the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 time of accident petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 34 years and was working as Coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Due to the grievous injuries,
prolonged treatment, he could not attend to his work and lost income.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Sarjapura Police have registered a case against rider of Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent, hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

Later, the counsel for the petitioner has filed application to implead respondents No.3 and 3 who are RC owner and insurer of Police vehicle and the same was allowed and permitted to implead respondents No.3 and 4.
Later inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.3 remained absent and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 respondent No.4 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. Respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied age, occupation, income of the petitioner, manner of the accident, negligence on the part of the rider of Motor Cycle, involvement of the Motor Cycle in the alleged accident, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that on verification of their records, it is found that the Yallamma has taken liability only policy for two-wheeler to her vehicle bearing No. KA-01-HX-8284 and the same is valid as on the date of accident and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and the rider of Motor Cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of the alleged accident and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated and hence pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.1 with costs.
05.

06 . On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues and additional Issues have been framed:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 09.07.2021 at about 09.25 a.m, near Maruthi Showroom.
Attibele, Sarjapura road, Sarjapura, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of riding of the Scooter bearing registration No.KA-01-HX-8284 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
( SCCH-3
03. What Order or Award?
ADDITIONAL ISSUES 01.
Whether the respondent No.4 proves that due to the negligence of the petitioner accident took place?
02. Whether respondent No.4 proves that the rider of the Honda Deo Motor Cycle not having valid driving license?

10. My findings on the above Issues and additional Issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 As per final order for the following:-
Additional Issue No.1 In the Negative Additional Issue No.2 In the Negative (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Further, stated that the driver of the Police vehicle Mallikarjuna who also sustained injuries in the accident in question, who had taken treatment in the said hospital, established that when he drove the same with high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner, in order to chase a chain snatches, lost control over the same and dashed to the road divider and also to the electric pole, which was on the middle of the road divider and as a result the electric pole, fell on the Tata Ace vehicle in which petitioner was travelling and sustained injuries in the accident.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.1 counsel he admits that he was proceeding in a Tata Ace vehicle and the Police came with high speed to catch the thief and they lost control and hit the divider, then the electric pole and the electric pole fell on him and that the Deo Motor Cycle No.KA-01-HX-8284 was not moving in front of the police.

(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 On perusal of the exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Sarjapura Police against rider of the Dio Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint shows that due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Dio Motor Cycle accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Sketch and Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on Attibele - Sarjapura Road, in between Gattanna's land and Srinivasa Reddy's land, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report which discloses that involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident and no damages found at the time of inspection.

Ex.P.6 is Wound certificate which Devendra vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166858572/
5 discloses that petitioner has sustained 1) Laceration over left parietal region of head, 2) Laceration over back of left ear and 3) Pain in neck.

sentences.text: MRI scan showed grade I anterior listhesis of C7 and D1 vertebra.

Fracture of spinosus process of C5, 6 and 7 with displacement cervical cord cyrinx at C6 vertebra and doctor has opined that injury No.3 is grievous in nature and injury Nos.1 and 2 are simple in nature.

Ex.P.7 is Charge sheet it discloses that the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against rider/respondent No.2 of Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 338 of IPC (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 and Sec.187 of IMV Act for the reasons the rider of the Motor Cycle after causing accident fled away from the accident spot.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner/respondent No.2 of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.9 is copy of Reply to notice given by the owner of the offending Motor Cycle has stated that he was riding the Motor Cycle and he had valid driving licence and said vehicle had valid insurance as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.10 is driving licence of respondent No.2.

Ex. P.13 is RC of Police vehicle.

Ex.P.18 is Spine report.
Ex.P.19 is Lab report.

The petitioner got examined Medical Records In-charge at Town hospital, as PW.2 and he has produced Authorization letter, Police intimation, MLC extract, Inpatient records and X-rays as per Ex.P.22 to 26, wherein it is mentioned that "H/O RTA, on 09.07.2021 at around 09.30 a.m on Sarjapura - (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 Attibele Road, near Maruthi Showroom, while going on Tata Ace".
In his cross-examination he stated that he do not know what was written in the documents he presented and admits that it does not say which vehicle caused the accident.

To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondent No.1 got examined Medical Records Officer at HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru, as RW.1 and she has produced Authorization letter, Wound certificate and MLC extract of driver of 112 Police vehicle as per Ex.R.1 to 3 which shows that the driver of 112 Police vehicle also sustained injuries and took treatment at HOSMAT hospital,
Bengaluru and it is further mentioned that "H/O RTA, (he was driving a Jeep, chasing a chain snatcher, hit a divider and jeep toppled, around 08.30 a.m on 09.07.2021 near Sarjapura Road".
In her cross-examination by the petitioner counsel she admits that Ex.R.2 is related to the injured Mallikarjun and it is not related to the applicant.

Further, the Senior Executive of the respondent No.1 Insurance Company is examined as RW.2 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the averments made in the objections and she has produced Authorization letter, Insurance policy and (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 Letter send to respondent No.2 along with postal cover as per Ex.R.4 to 6 which shows that the respondent No.1 send a letter to Mrs.Yallamma to provide vehicular documents to vehicle No.KA-01-HX-8284 and the policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force and which stands in the name of Devendra vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166858572/
6 said Yallamma as on the date of accident.

In her cross-examination she admits that Motor Cycle No.
KA-01-HX-8284 was insured at the time of the accident and Police have filed a final report on the rider of the said vehicle.

Though the Charge sheet is filed against rider of the offending Motor Cycle, but on perusal of entire oral and documentary evidence adduced by both the parties clearly goes to show that, the accident has also occurred due to negligence of driver of 112 Police vehicle who was proceeding at high speed,
in rash and negligent manner to catch the thief and took right turn and dashed to the road divider and then to electric pole and the electric pole fell on the Tata Ace vehicle in which petitioner was travelling and sustained injuries.
Therefore, it is clear that there is equal contributory negligence on the part of rider of Honda Dio Motor Cycle and driver of 112 Police vehicle this accident occurred.

Accordingly, apportion of the negligence at (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 the ratio of 50% -
50% on the part of the rider of the Motor Cycle and driver of the 112 Police vehicle.
Accordingly, I have answered the Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.
12. Additional Issues No.1 and 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these additional Issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13. The respondent No.4 has taken specific contention that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and rider of the Honda Deo Motor Cycle not having valid driving licence.

On perusal of Charge sheet, it is found that the Investigation Officer has not stated anything regarding accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner because the petitioner was proceeding in Tata Ace vehicle in which electrical pole broken and fallen on the said vehicle and has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the rider of Honda Dio Motor Cycle.
In this regard, the respondent No.4 did not lead evidence to prove its contention.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.4 is untenable.
Accordingly, additional Issues No.1 and 2 are answered in the negative.

(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 14. Issue No.2:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.
PW.1 in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 34 years and was working as Coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, treatment and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost his income, earning capacity and become permanent disabled.
15. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.17 Aadhaar card.

Even though the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1986 and the alleged accident was occurred on 09.07.2021.

Therefore, considering the said documents, this Devendra vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166858572/
7 tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 35 years.

As per the ratio laid down (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16'.
16.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/- and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained laceration wound over the parietal region, laceration over the left ear, anterior listhesis of C7 over D1, fracture of the spinous process of C5, C6 and C7 with displacement with cervical cord at C6 vertebra and this petitioner falls in the iii a) category, hence he has a disability of 10% and he has produced Clinical report and X-ray as per Ex.P.27 and 28.

In his (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and he has not assessed the functional disability and fracture is united and petitioner taken conservative treatment.

He has not produce the radiological report and denied to the suggestion that petitioner sustained only simple injury hence he was treated conservatively and denied to the suggestion that since the fracture is united, the complaint mentioned in para 5 and 6 does not arise.
He has assessed whole body disability.

However,
considering the evidence of PW.3, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records,
this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 16 x 10%/100 = Rs.2,88,000/-.
18.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries of Town hospital, Sarjapur and Balaji Nursing Home, Dommasandra, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 14 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.

19. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.4 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and as per Inpatient records, Clinical report, X-rays and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

20. Loss of income during laid up period:- As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,000/- p.m and she was admitted in the hospital for 14 days as inpatient.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
(Rs.15,000 x 2) under this head.
21. Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced entire Medical bills and Prescriptions as per (SCCH-3) 20 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 Ex.P.16 and 20 for Rs.69,309/-.

To disprove the medical bills,
the respondents have not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.69,309/- under this head.
22. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
23. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl. Head of compensation Amount in Rs. No.
1 . Loss of future income 2,88,000-00 2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
3. Attendant charges, extra nutritious 30,000-00 food and conveyance charges
4. Medical Expenses 69,309-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00 unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 30,000-00 period Total 4,77,309-00 (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.4484/2021 24.
Regarding liability:-

As discussed in the Issue No.1, this tribunal already held that due to contributory negligence of the rider of Motor Cycle and driver of 112 Police vehicle this accident occurred, hence the negligence is taken at the ratio of 50% - 50% respectively.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the insurer and RC owner of the Honda Dio Motor Cycle and respondents No.3 and 4 being the RC owner and insurer of the 112 Police vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since the policy of the Motor Cycle and 112 Police vehicle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondents No.1 and 4 being the insurers of the said vehicles shall deposit the above said compensation amount equally with interest within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

25. Issue No.3:- In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,77,309/- (Rupees Four lakhs seventy seven thousand three hundred and nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.1 and 4 shall deposit above said compensation amount equally with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

9 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,77,309/- (Rupees Four lakhs seventy seven thousand three hundred and nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.1 and 4 shall deposit above said compensation amount equally with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
